newsitem.title: USA: CBOT WHEAT CLOSES HIGHER ON WORLD WEATHER PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: CBOT WHEAT CLOSES HIGHER ON WORLD WEATHER PROBLEMS.

text.p: Mounting concerns about potential declines in production in some areas and quality in other parts of the world due to harsh weather boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.

"We keep hearing more about Canada's crop shrinking, problems in Australia and in Europe with the rains and flooding there are concerns about quality," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp.
Wheat found support at the end of the week on a Canadian Wheat Board outlook for a wheat corp in western Canada this year of 21.6 million tonnes, below the 29.5 million produced last year.

The Australian Wheat Board Friday said Australia's domestic wheat market continues to be driven by crop concerns in dry parts of the southern and eastern states and Romanian officials Friday said heavy rains, hail and floods recently turned bumper wheat crops into fodder on thousands of hectares.
ADM Investor Services was a late buyer of three million bushels which boosted wheat to the day's highs at the close.
CBOT soft red winter wheat closed one to six cents per bushel higher, with September up four at $3.67-1/4.
Traders said a recovery in corn futures and a late rally in soybeans helped boost wheat futures.
USDA's weekly export sales report this week was supportive for wheat and there talk continued that Egypt may be in the market this weekend for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes of wheat.
Gains were limited by the large supply of U.S. winter wheat that continued to become readily available to the marketing pipeline during rallies in wheat futures markets.

USDA Tuesday will release its August crop production report and supply/demand report. An average of analysts' estimates pegged 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.476 billion bushels, above USDA's July forecast for 2.431 billion.

In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did one million bushels of December/September at 14-3/4 to 15 cents, premium December and Merrill Lynch Futures spread one million September/December at 15 cents, premium December.

FIMAT Futures bought 2.5 million bushels of December and sold one million December, traders said. Term Commodities sold 1.5 million December and Refco Inc bought 1.3 million December and sold 300,000 bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 19,000 contracts, below the 28,006 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 200 September $3.60 calls at 12-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures sold 200 December $3.80 calls at 19-1/2 cents and sold 200 December $3.80 puts at 18-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000, below the 8,223 traded Thursday.
